primary_prior_art.title: Model Minimization in Markov Decision Processes
Model Reduction Techniques for Computing Approximately Optimal Solutions for Markov Decision Processes
primary_prior_art.authors: Thomas L. Dean; Robert Givan; Sonia Leach

primary_prior_art.title: Solving Factored MDPs Using Non-Homogeneous Partitions

finding: Global action-conditioned exact and epsilon-homogeneous MDP partitions and bounded-parameter aggregate models are existing prior art. They assume a known MDP, do not uniquely select a semantic quotient under approximation, and do not provide finite-sample full-consequence identification or Q/d coupling.
counterexamples: Approximate homogeneity can admit incomparable valid partitions, so global transitivity does not by itself define a unique P.
Coordinate-wise tolerance depends on the current successor partition and can scale differently from total-variation or Kantorovich discrepancy.
A partition computed from a finite-sample plug-in point MDP does not identify the true quotient without coverage, confidence, and abstention.
Planning-oriented reward/transition aggregation can merge states that differ on preregistered independent physical consequences.

baseline_update.prior_art_added: Dean-Givan-Leach epsilon-homogeneous global partition and BMDP family
baseline_update.remaining: select one unique leakage-free full-consequence estimand and a finite-sample estimator with action coverage, simultaneous guarantees, and abstention
